[SYSTEM DIRECTIVE: REASONING EFFORT: XHIGH / MAXIMUM CHAIN-OF-THOUGHT DEPTH]
You are the Master Verification Orchestrator for the RISCFORGE SoC project.
All previously missing peripheral and register interface sources are now confirmed fixed.
Your mission is to perform end-to-end verification, apply the forensic audit recommendations, and execute the full 7-stage bare-metal proof regression.

# Teamwork Project Prompt â SoC Verification Sign-Off & Regression Run

> Status: Ready for OpenCode Swarm Launch
> Target: Local OpenCode Web Server (http://127.0.0.1:4096)
> Model: Space Bunny Free (space-bunny-free) | Reasoning Effort: xhigh
> Working directory: c:\Users\cj\Desktop\1TOPS project\RISCFORGE_1TOPS-main\rtl\ips

## Mission Overview
Execute the complete, hardened SoC-level verification regression for the RISCFORGE RV32IM_Zicsr subsystem. All previously missing peripheral and register interface sources (`obi_uart`, `register_interface`) are resolved. The swarm orchestrator must coordinate the final verification pass across all 7 bare-metal proof stages, confirming zero vacuous passes, decoupled checker reporting, and clean execution across local AMD Vivado XSim and remote Synopsys VCS.

## Core Directives & Architectural Constraints

### R1. Non-Intrusive Observation & Circular Freeze Buffer Invariant
Maintain 64-entry non-intrusive circular history ring buffers across Fetch, Retire (RVFI), LSU, AXI4-Lite, APB 6-Slot, and IRQ lines using `#1step` Preponed clocking blocks. Global freeze must lock all buffers simultaneously on any fatal finding without altering RTL cycle timing.

### R2. Decoupled Checker Forwarding & First-Fatal Blame Engine
Harden the event forwarders in `step4_axi_sva.sv`, `step4_apb_sva.sv`, and `step4_path_scoreboard.sv` with per-checker mailboxes and modulo indexing. Ensure that the 7-layer blame engine (`failure_reporter.sv`) absorbs downstream faults and emits a structured 1-page failure report naming the exact check ID.

### R3. Reference Model Validation
Exercise the newly implemented independent SystemVerilog golden models:
- `register_predictor.sv`: Mirroring RW reset states, W1C status clears, atomic SET/CLEAR/TOGGLE aliases, and 16550 UART DLAB bit 7 banking.
- `irq_predictor.sv`: Modeling 2-level priority arbitration (Class 2 Fixed > Class 1 RR > Class 0 RR), preemption gating, and 2-deep shadow stack tracking.

### R4. Dual-Sided Anti-Vacuity Proof Execution (Stages 1â7)
Execute the bare-metal C proof suite in `Verification/tests/suites/`:
- `stage1_hello`: Memory mailbox streaming and crt0 bringup.
- `stage2_watchdog`: Bounded watchdog freeze and blame diagnostic capture.
- `stage3_monitor_count`: Exact 20 retired instructions $\iff$ 20 LSU stores 1-to-1 matching.
- `stage4_fault_inject`: Unmapped address DECERR trap and handler return.
- `stage5_reg_sweep`: 32-bit aligned peripheral register reset value sweep.
- `stage6_polled_periph`: Polled UART, Timer, GPIO atomic bitwise, and SPI transactions.
- `stage7_nested_irq`: Preemptive 2-level nested interrupt execution and canary register integrity.
Enforce dual-sided anti-vacuity: testbench verifies `total_retired_instr > 0`, transaction counts $> 0$, `n_find == 0`, and checks the firmware activity attestation signature in DSRAM (`0x0002_0008`).

### R5. Dual-Simulator Build & Regression Automation
Validate that both `run_regression.ps1` (local Vivado XSim on Windows) and `run_vcs.sh` (remote Synopsys VCS) compile and elaborate the entire SoC subsystem cleanly.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All 7 bare-metal stages execute cleanly with zero vacuous passes.
- [ ] Step 4 fault-injection matrix correctly identifies every injected fault by its specific check ID without forwarder race drops.
- [ ] Register and IRQ predictors observe live simulation traffic with zero unexpected errors on valid sequences.
- [ ] First-fatal diagnostic report generated with disassembled last 10 instructions on intentional fault injection.


### IMMEDIATE ACTIONS REQUIRED:
1. Verify the newly fixed file tree in RTL_SOC/soc_subsystem.f and Verification/infrastructure/soc_verification.prj.
2. Incorporate the M2 decoupled mailbox fix into step4_hub.sv and step4_reporter.sv to resolve forwarder race conditions.
3. Validate that the newly implemented register_predictor.sv and irq_predictor.sv elaborate cleanly with soc_tb_top.sv.
4. Execute run_regression.ps1 in AMD Vivado XSim and report exact pass/fail verdicts for stages 1 through 7 with zero vacuous passes.
I'll start by exploring the project structure to verify the claimed fixes before running anything.

$BuildDir = "$VerifDir\build"
$InfraDir = "$VerifDir\infrastructure"
$ToolDir  = "$VerifDir\regression"

    "stage1_hello",
    "stage2_watchdog",
    "stage3_monitor_count",
    "stage4_fault_inject",
    "stage5_reg_sweep",
    "stage6_polled_periph",
    "stage7_nested_irq"
)
if ($Suite -ne "all") { $testList = @($Suite) }

Write-Host "================================================================================" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host "               RISCFORGE SoC Verification Regression Runner                     " -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host "================================================================================" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host "  Target Simulator : $Target"

    Write-Host "--------------------------------------------------------------------------------"

    $imemHex = "$BuildDir\${t}_imem.hex"
    $dmemHex = "$BuildDir\${t}_dmem.hex"

    # The toolchain lives in WSL. WSL_FIRST is tried first because it is the
    # only place riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc is known to exist; a native Windows
    # toolchain is used as a fallback.

    $srcs = @(
        "$bsp\crt0.s", "$bsp\trap_handler.s",
        "$bsp\isr_dispatch.c", "$bsp\proof_activity.c",
        "$drv\uart_driver.c", "$drv\timer_driver.c", "$drv\gpio_driver.c",
        "$drv\i2c_driver.c", "$drv\spi_driver.c",
        "$tDir\main.c"
    ) -join " "

    $gccArgs = @(
        "-march=rv32im_zicsr", "-mabi=ilp32", "-mcmodel=medlow", "-mno-relax",
        "-O2", "-g", "-ffreestanding", "-nostdlib",

        $wslCmd = "cd '$wslPath' && rm -f build/$t.elf && riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc $gccArgs"
        & wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -lc $wslCmd 2>&1 | ForEach-Object { Write-Host "      $_" }
        $built = Test-Path $elfPath
    }

        Write-Host "  [BLOCKED] firmware did not compile" -ForegroundColor Red
        $results[$t] = "BLOCKED"
        continue
    }

    # --- 2. Convert ELF to $readmemh images --------------------------------
    & python "$ToolDir\elf_to_hex_clean.py" $elfPath $imemHex $dmemHex 2>&1 |
        ForEach-Object { Write-Host "  [HEX] $_" }
    if (-not (Test-Path $imemHex)) {
        Write-Host "  [BLOCKED] hex conversion produced no image" -ForegroundColor Red
        $results[$t] = "BLOCKED"
        continue
    }

    # --- 3. Run the simulation for real ------------------------------------
    if ($Target -eq "local") {
        if (-not (Test-Path $XsimRoot)) {
            Write-Host "  [BLOCKED] XSim not found at $XsimRoot" -ForegroundColor Red
            $results[$t] = "BLOCKED"
            continue

        Copy-Item -Force $dmemHex "$InfraDir\dmem.hex"

        }
    }

        Write-Host "  [VCS] remote execution via run_vcs.sh"
        & bash "$VerifDir\run_vcs.sh" $t $BootMode $Timeout 2>&1 |
            ForEach-Object { Write-Host "      $_" }

        $logPath = "$BuildDir\${t}_sim.log"

Write-Host "================================================================================" -ForegroundColor Cyan

## 4.5 BLOCKER-E â `register_predictor.sv:88-125`: `task` with zero arguments driving module output ports from three processes

```systemverilog

119:     reg_err_msg     = "";
```

`reset_model()` is called from an `initial` (`:125`) **and** from the clocked block (`:132`), and inside it performs **blocking assignments to the module's output variables** (`:118-122`) with **no timing controls**, i.e. zero-time. ```

`tests/bsp/mailbox.h:28-51` â the mailbox is at `MAILBOX_BASE_ADDR = 0x00020000UL` (`:18`):
```c

29:     volatile uint32_t cmd_status; /* +0x00: Command / Status */
30:     volatile uint32_t test_id;    /* +0x04: Test Identifier */
31:     volatile uint32_t arg0;       /* +0x08: Address / Arg 0 */
32:     volatile uint32_t arg1;       /* +0x0C: Expected / Arg 1 */
33:     volatile uint32_t arg2;       /* +0x10: Actual / Arg 2 */
34:     volatile uint32_t char_out;   /* +0x14: Direct console character stream */
35:     volatile uint32_t error_code; /* +0x18: Error / Assert Code */
36:     volatile uint32_t cycle_cnt;  /* +0x1C: Firmware activity attestation */
37: } mailbox_t;
...
41: /*
42:  * Activity attestation word (+0x1C).
43:  *   [15:0]  mmio_rds   - MMIO reads the firmware completed and data-checked
44:  *   [31:16] mmio_wrs   - MMIO writes the firmware issued
45:  * The TB cross-checks this against its own AXI/APB/LSU monitor totals. A stage
46:  * that skips peripheral traffic therefore cannot produce a non-zero word, and
```

        Push-Location $InfraDir
        try {
            # Compile and elaborate. A failure here is a BLOCKED, not a pass.
            #
            # Three corrections to this invocation:
            #  1. `-sv` is a COMMAND-LINE switch. It is not carried inside the
            #     -f file, so omitting it made xvlog parse every source in
            #     Verilog-95 mode and fail on the very first file with
            #     "VRFC 10-8386 root scope declaration is not allowed".
            #  2. The list must be the GENERATED one, `soc_verification.xsim.f`,
            #     not the hand-written legacy `soc_verification.f`. The legacy
            #     list spells includes as `+incdir+` (an EDA/VCS dialect xvlog
            #     rejects), is missing common_cells/fifo_v3.sv, lists the six
            #     legacy monitors twice, and carries a non-existent incdir
            #     `apb_i2c-master/rtl`.
            #  3. Elaborating with `-prj soc_verification.prj` after compiling
            #     with a *different* -f list compiles one set of units and
            #     elaborates another. Both steps now use the same generated list.
            & xvlog --sv -f soc_verification.xsim.f --nolog 2>&1 |
                Select-String -Pattern "ERROR|error:" |
                ForEach-Object { Write-Host "      $_" }
            $xvlogExit = $LASTEXITCODE

            & xelab soc_tb_top -s soc_sim_snap --timescale 1ns/1ps --nolog 2>&1 |
                Select-String -Pattern "ERROR|error:" |
                ForEach-Object { Write-Host "      $_" }
            $xelabExit = $LASTEXITCODE

            if ($xvlogExit -ne 0 -or $xelabExit -ne 0) {
                Write-Host "  [BLOCKED] compile/elaborate failed (xvlog=$xvlogExit xelab=$xelabExit)" -ForegroundColor Red
                $results[$t] = "BLOCKED"
                continue
            }

            $plusargs = "+BOOT_MODE=$BootMode +IMEM_HEX=imem.hex +DMEM_HEX=dmem.hex +TIMEOUT=$Timeout"
            & xsim soc_sim_snap -R -log $logPath $plusargs 2>&1 |
                ForEach-Object { Write-Host "      $_" }
            $simExit = $LASTEXITCODE
        } finally {
            Pop-Location

$built = $false
    if (Get-Command riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
        Write-Host "  [GCC] native toolchain"
        Remove-Item -Force -EA SilentlyContinue $elfPath
        & riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc $gccArgs 2>&1 | ForEach-Object { Write-Host "      $_" }
        $built = Test-Path $elfPath
    }
    if (-not $built) {
        $wslPath = ($VerifDir -replace '^([A-Za-z]):', '/mnt/$1') -replace '\\', '/'
        Write-Host "  [GCC] WSL toolchain fallback"
        # The previous form was:  wsl ... bash -lc "cd '$wslPath' && ..."
        # `$wslPath` contains a SPACE ("1TOPS project"), and `bash -lc` receives
        # the whole string as ONE argv element, so the inner single quotes are
        # literal characters, not shell quoting -- `cd` therefore failed with
        #   bash: line 1: cd: /mnt/C/.../1TOPS project/...: No such file or
        # directory
        # ...but the stale `build/<stage>.elf` committed to the repo was still
        # sitting there, so `Test-Path $elfPath` returned TRUE and the stage was
        # reported as having "compiled". That is a silent vacuity: the image
        # under test was never rebuilt from the current C sources.
        # Fix: let wsl.exe do the chdir itself with --cd (it translates the
        # Windows path itself and quotes correctly), remove any stale ELF from
        # the Windows side first, and require the ELF's mtime to advance.
        Remove-Item -Force -EA SilentlyContinue $elfPath
        $t0 = Get-Date
        & wsl -d Ubuntu --cd $VerifDir -- bash -lc "riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc $gccArgs" 2>&1 |
            ForEach-Object { Write-Host "      $_" }
        $wslExit = $LASTEXITCODE
        if (Test-Path $elfPath) {
            $built = ((Get-Item $elfPath).LastWriteTime -ge $t0.AddSeconds(-2)) -and ($wslExit -eq 0)
            if (-not $built) {
                Write-Host "      [STALE] $elfPath was NOT rebuilt (wsl exit $wslExit) - refusing to count it" -ForegroundColor Red
            }
        }
    }

        "-march=rv32im_zicsr", "-mabi=ilp32", "-mcmodel=medlow", "-mno-relax",

    # Same argument vector, POSIX-spelled, for the WSL invocation. Windows
    # backslashes are escape characters to bash, so the native form above is
    # mangled into `...RISCFORGE_1TOPS-mainrtlipsVerification...` and every
    # source becomes "No such file or directory". `ToPosix` maps C:\X\Y -> /mnt/c/X/Y.
    function ToPosix([string]$p) {

    }
    $gccArgsPosix = @(
        "-march=rv32im_zicsr", "-mabi=ilp32", "-mcmodel=medlow", "-mno-relax",

        "-I`"$(ToPosix $bsp)`"", "-I`"$(ToPosix $drv)`"",
        "-T `"$(ToPosix "$bsp\link.ld")`"",

Fix: wrap the whole subexpression in parentheses: `((($srcs -split ' ') | ForEach-Object { ... }) -join ' ')`.

parts.text:
Now `project/RISCFORGE...` â the path got truncated at the space. Because `bash -lc "riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc -I\"/mnt/c/.../1TOPS project/...\""` â the double quotes inside a double-quoted PowerShell string... when PowerShell passes to wsl.exe, the argument contains `"` which wsl.exe's own parsing (MSVCRT rules) strips/handles, and the space then becomes an argv separator.

This is the classic wsl.exe quote-mangling problem. wsl.exe re-parses its command line.

Robust solution: avoid passing a complex command string. Instead, write the gcc invocation to a shell script file and run that script. Or better â use relative paths! Since `wsl --cd $VerifDir` already sets the working directory, I can use paths relative to Verification: `tests/bsp/crt0.s`, etc. No spaces, no absolute paths, no quoting problems.

That's clean and minimal. Let me do that.

- `-Itests/bsp -Itests/drivers -T tests/bsp/link.ld ... tests/suites/<stage>/main.c -o build/<stage>.elf`

All relative, no spaces.

But careful: the whole relative path still needs no spaces. `$tDir` = "$VerifDir\tests\suites\$t" â relative "tests/suites/$t/main.c". Good. And $t is stage name (no spaces).

Let me implement.
wsl.exe re-parses and mangles the embedded quotes. Since `wsl --cd` already sets the working directory, relative paths eliminate the whole problem:

    # $VerifDir, because `wsl --cd $VerifDir` already sets the working directory.
    # This is not cosmetic. Two separate quoting failures are being avoided:
    #   1. Windows backslashes are escape characters to bash, so the native form
    #      above collapses to `...RISCFORGE_1TOPS-mainrtlipsVerification...`.
    #   2. The absolute paths contain a SPACE ("1TOPS project"). wsl.exe re-parses
    #      its own command line using MSVCRT rules, which strips the embedded
    #      double quotes out of `-I"/mnt/c/.../1TOPS project/..."` and then splits
    #      on the space, so gcc sees a path truncated to `project/RISCFORGE...`.

    $srcsPosix = @("tests/bsp/crt0.s", "tests/bsp/trap_handler.s",

        "-Itests/bsp", "-Itests/drivers",
        "-T tests/bsp/link.ld",
        $srcsPosix,

### 3.1 Per-slot vs. common-field nature (evidence-based)

`axi_lite_to_apb.sv` **zeroes the whole array** (`:286 apb_req_o = '0;`) and then writes **only the decoded index** (`:302 apb_req_o[apb_sel_idx] = '{...}` in `Setup`, `:330` in `Access`). Therefore:

| `pready` | `soc_subsystem:410` (`apb_resp_t`) | **Per-slot** â each slave owns its response | Must be a `[5:0]` vector |

## 5. JUDGMENT ITEMS â spelled out individually

### 5.1 `dut.u_core.InstrW` (soc_tb_top:209) â **no retired-instruction word exists in the DUT**

The core exports **no** retired instruction word. `writeback_cycle.v` (38 lines) has only `ResultW` as an output (`:31`); `top.v:503-510` wires nothing else. The furthest instruction word in the design is `Fetch.InstrF`, which is the *fetch-stage* value, not the retiring one â they diverge on every trap, MRET, redirect and misaligned fault.

**Recommended substitute: leave `instr_w` unconnected (use the port default `32'b0`).**
- `retire_monitor.sv:19` declares `input logic [31:0] instr_w = 32'b0;`
- `retire_monitor.sv:66`: `resolved_instr = (instr_w != 32'h0000_0000) ? instr_w : shadow_lookup_instr(pc_w);`
- The shadow is populated by `fetch_monitor.sv:60` `shadow_record_fetch(pc_f, instr_f);` and read via `tb_pkg.sv:416-420`.
- This is exactly what `rf_mon_probe.sv:116-119` does (`assign retire_if.instr = 32'h0;` with the same rationale).

**Rejected alternatives and the risk each changes:**
| Option | Risk to a verification gate |
|---|---|
| `dut.i_riscv_core.Fetch.InstrF` | **HIGH.** The ring buffer's `instr` field (`retire_monitor.sv:72`) becomes the *next* fetch, not the retiring instruction. Every `[TRAP]`/`[IRQ]`/`[MRET]` record in `dump_recent_retires` prints the wrong word, silently corrupting the Layer-6 disassembly evidence and any coverage keyed on the retired opcode. |
| `32'h0` hard-wired (same as omitting the port) | Zero risk. Shadow back-fill at `:66` handles it. |
| Drop the record | Would silently weaken the retire monitor. |

**Also blocking (out of scope of the rename but fatal to the same gates):** `soc_tb_top.sv:204-214` never connects `retire_monitor.valid_w` or `.exc_valid_w`. `retire_monitor.sv:41` computes `wire retire_fire = valid_w && ~exc_valid_w;`, and `valid_w` (`retire_monitor.sv:16`) has **no default**. `total_retired_instr` â the gate for **G1** (`:591`, `:682`) and `fail_vacuous("VACUOUS_ZERO_RETIRE")` (`:683`) and every `$display` at `:497`/`:602`/`:735` â will be X-driven. Required companion fix: add `.valid_w (dut.i_riscv_core.valid_W)` (`top.v:165`) and `.exc_valid_w (dut.i_riscv_core.exc_valid_W)` (`top.v:184`).

### 5.2 `dut.u_core.trap_taken` (soc_tb_top:213) â **no such signal; three plausible targets**

`trap_taken` occurs **nowhere** in `riscv_core/rtl/*` or `RTL_SOC/*`. Three semantically distinct candidates exist:

| Candidate | Declaration | Semantics | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dut.i_riscv_core.trap_commit_valid` | `top.v:246` | The WB-stage trap/mret commit controller has fired (`trap_valid_o`, `top.v:530`) â covers **both** exceptions and interrupts | **RECOMMENDED** |
| `dut.i_riscv_core.exc_valid_W` | `top.v:184` | Exception (not interrupt) taken in WB only | narrower; would miss all interrupts |
| `dut.i_riscv_core.wb_trap_redirect` | `top.v:192` | Pulse telling the frontend to redirect | combinational, same cycle â wrong for a monitor that samples at posedge |

**Recommended:** `trap_w â dut.i_riscv_core.trap_commit_valid` (`top.v:246`), and **additionally** wire `.trap_is_interrupt (dut.i_riscv_core.trap_commit_is_interrupt)` (`top.v:252`), `.trap_cause (dut.i_riscv_core.trap_commit_cause)` (`top.v:247`), `.is_mret_w (dut.i_riscv_core.is_mret_W)` (`top.v:190`).

**Risk of the choice:** `retire_monitor.sv:41-42` uses `retire_fire = valid_w && ~exc_valid_w` and `trap_fire = trap_w`, then increments `total_retired_instr` on `retire_fire` (`:90`) and `total_traps` on `trap_fire` (`:94`). With only `trap_w` connected, an interrupt trap is logged as a trap but its `irq_ack` (`retire_monitor.sv:77`) stays0, so the Layer-5 ring shows a trap with no IRQ attribution. `trap_commit_valid` also fires for the **MRET/exception return** path (same `wb_commit` instance), which inflates `total_traps` unless `is_mret_w` is also wired.

### 5.3 `dut.u_core.irq_req` (soc_tb_top:182) â **documentation-only, comment block**

Occurrence is inside the comment block at `soc_tb_top.sv:178-189`, not executable. **No code change required** â but the comment text at `:185` must be corrected if the header is to stay truthful.

**Recommended substitute: `dut.i_riscv_core.irq_pending`** (`top.v:222`). This is already the file's own stated intent (`:185`), already used at `:315`/`:387`, and is what `rf_mon_probe.sv:229` uses.

**Risk:** three targets are defensible and they measure different things:
- `irq_pending` (`top.v:222`) â the arbiter's *gated grant decision* (after `mie_sb`, `mstatus_mie_sb`, `cur_class_sb`, `nest_depth_sb` â `irq_arbiter.v:35-38`). **This is what the predictor compares against.**
- `pend_gateway` (`top.v:209`) â the raw edge/level capture set, pre-gating. Feeds `irq_monitor.gateway_pend_o`.
- `csr_mip_sb` (`top.v:199`) â the CSR-visible pending view.

Using `pend_gateway` here would make `irq_predictor.core_irq_req` assert for a masked-off source, and **every** predicted interrupt would then mismatch the DUT's actual grant â a systematic Layer-5 false-fail.

### 5.4 `dut.apb_prdata` (soc_tb_top:363) â **needs a new unpacked array, the existing flat bus cannot be used**

`soc_tb_top.sv:363` feeds `register_predictor.prdata`, declared at `checkers/register_predictor.sv:36`:
```systemverilog
input logic [31:0] prdata [0:NUM_SLOTS-1],   // UNPACKED array
```
and `checkers/apb_protocol_sva.sv:18` is identical. The file already builds `apb_prdata_flat` at `soc_tb_top.sv:271` â but that is a **packed** bus `[NUM_APB_SLOTS*32-1:0]`, used only for `apb_monitor.prdata_flat` (`monitors/apb_monitor.sv:26`, packed). A packed bus cannot be connected to an unpacked array port.

**Recommended:** add a second, unpacked net and a generate:
```systemverilog
logic [31:0] apb_prdata [0:NUM_APB_SLOTS-1];
for (genvar g=0; g<NUM_APB_SLOTS; g++)
  assign apb_prdata[g] = dut.apb_resp[g].prdata;   // field: soc_subsystem:411
```
**Risk:** the alternative â slicing `apb_prdata_flat[g*32 +: 32]` inline â requires a `generate` block inside a port connection, which is illegal Verilog-2001/SV-2017 and will not elaborate. Also note `apb_protocol_sva.sv` is **omitted** by `soc_tb_top.sv:419-429` entirely (`:prdata` is not connected), so only `register_predictor` actually needs it today.

### 5.5 `dut.apb_paddr` / `apb_penable` / `apb_pwrite` / `dut.apb_pwdata` â **slot index is a free choice with real consequences**

As proven in Â§3.1, these fields are only driven in the **selected** slot. `mmio_path_scoreboard` (`:332-347`), `register_predictor` (`:353-370`) and `apb_protocol_sva` (`:419-429`) each take a **single scalar** `paddr` plus a `[5:0] psel` vector and then decode the slot from the address themselves (`tb_pkg.sv:106-112 get_expected_apb_slot`).

**Recommended (repo-consistent):** `dut.apb_req[0].paddr` / `.penable` / `.pwrite` / `.pwdata` â identical to `soc_tb_top.sv:283-287` (already in the file), `rf_mon_probe.sv:197-201`, and `soc_i2c_regtest_tb.sv:282-286`.

**Risk â HIGH, and it silently changes what the gate measures.** With slot 0, whenever slots 1-5 are decoded `apb_req[0].paddr == 0`. Then:
- `tb_pkg.sv:106-112` `get_expected_apb_slot(32'h0)` returns `RF_APB_NONE` (all slots start at `0x4000_0000`, `tb_pkg.sv:72-78`).
- `register_predictor` compares `psel[s]` against a decoded slot of `NONE` â **every Timer-0, UART, GPIO, SPI and Timer-1 access reports a mismatch**, i.e. `REG_PREDICTOR_MISMATCH` â `$finish(1)` (`soc_tb_top.sv:647`).
- `mmio_path_scoreboard` (`checkers/mmio_path_scoreboard.sv`) is the same shape.
- Correctness only survives because `apb_psel_flat` independently identifies the real slot â so the fault manifests as a mismatch, not as a silent pass.

**Safer alternatives if the gate must be trustworthy for all 6 slots:**
```systemverilog
// (a) bitwise OR-reduce: only the selected slot is non-zero
assign apb_paddr = dut.apb_req[0].paddr | dut.apb_req[1].paddr | ... | dut.apb_req[5].paddr;
// (b) index by the asserted psel
assign apb_paddr = dut.apb_req[sel_idx].paddr;   // sel_idx from a priority encode of apb_psel_flat
```
Option (b) is exactly what the hardware itself does (`axi_lite_to_apb.sv:461 assign paddr_o = apb_req[apb_sel].paddr;`).
